# GB x LeoVegas Regroup
Date: 2026-09-30 | Duration: 42.720001220703125m

## Summary
The discussion covered the interim data pipeline, which uses DTM, Mixpanel, and a warehouse while awaiting the Group API, alongside a DBT migration toward the finalized data architecture. Feature-flag migration from LaunchDarkly was largely complete, with integrations across sportsbook, landing pages, and mobile apps. GrowthBook experimentation rollout remains dependent on product-manager enablement, with planned training using company-specific examples, prior experiments, practical exercises, and clear limits around unavailable features. Experimentation is being incorporated into the Product Development Lifecycle, combining legacy LaunchDarkly processes with sportsbook practices. Product teams will own ideation and setup, while experimentation specialists provide consultation and governance. Checklists, metric groups, templates, dashboards, and workflow prompts will support lightweight self-service. The discussion also covered soft stops, sample-size stopping, Slack notifications, and phase-date behavior to improve result consistency and issue detection. Contextual Bandits were deferred until core experimentation practices are established.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, Experimentation governance, Product manager self-service, Mixpanel integration, Experiment lifecycle, Contextual bandits

# GB x LeoVegas:  Intros & Enablement Planning
Date: 2026-10-06 | Duration: 32.099998474121094m

## Summary
GrowthBook support for LeoVegas will be led by Cris Dizon, with help available for strategy, experiment design, technical coordination, data support, engineering, and data questions. Chris Cassar leads the LeoVegas Data Product team, which supports data engineering, data science, BI, analysis, dashboards, pipelines, feature monitoring, roadmaps, sprints, and backlog management. LeoVegas is moving from LaunchDarkly toward broader GrowthBook use across multiple apps and product surfaces, with self-service experimentation as a key goal. Teams should eventually configure, launch, and analyze experiments independently, supported by playbooks, training, Slack coordination, recordings, and possibly an ambassador group. Product requirements will include data and experimentation prompts earlier in development. Training will begin with GrowthBook navigation, feature flags, and core experimentation workflows, followed by power calculations, experiment interpretation, and playbooks. Separate one-hour sessions are planned for engineering and product audiences, while Cris Dizon, Chris Cassar, Denny, and Joanna will coordinate process, culture, scheduling, and ongoing enablement.

## Keywords
Experimentation enablement, GrowthBook, Feature flags, Product development lifecycle, Statistical analysis, Self-service analytics
